scenes.name: Saturday Morning

beats.caption: Year nine. Director now. Saturday was supposed to stay quiet.

say: Boss. Help desk handed an attacker a password.
Caller said they were IT. The agent believed them.
Those credentials opened our internal admin tool.
They are inside customer accounts. This is live.
I'm on the bridge. We need a verb, not a meeting.
Shut the admin tool down. Cut every session.
Killing it. Customers will stumble. So will the attacker.
Revoke the bad access. Leave the tool standing.
Quiet revoke is running. I'll watch for a second door.
Get Elena first. No changes until she answers.
She'll want a verb. Have one when she picks up.
Clock's running. I kill the tool unless you stop me.

scenes.shot_notes: A phone buzzes by a cold mug. Sam appears on the screen in a dark SOC, energy drink in hand, while Marcus joins by speaker.

scenes.name: The Screenshot

beats.caption: Year nine. Security Director. A Saturday with nothing on the calendar.

say: Boss, you up? Open the screenshot I just sent.

beats.caption: A customer's public post: a Harborline email with a stranger's balance and home address pasted in.

say: That's our assistant. Priya's assistant. It wrote that email.
A teller asked it to draft a reply. It pulled a different customer's account.
It can read customer records. It was never supposed to.
The post is spreading. Give Sam a first move, then we talk.
Turn the assistant off. Every seat, every team.
Off in five. The whole bank just lost its favorite toy.
Cut what it can read. Leave the chat box up.
Pulling its access to the records. It's about to get a lot dumber.
Elena hears this from me before she sees that post.
Fine. Bring her a plan along with the bad news.
Nobody's stopping me, so I'm pulling the plug.

scenes.shot_notes: A phone buzzes face down beside a cold mug. You flip it. Sam fills the screen from a dark SOC, energy drink in hand, and Marcus joins on speaker.

scenes.name: Saturday Morning

beats.caption: Year nine. Security Director. Saturday was supposed to stay quiet.

say: Boss. Somebody's inside, and they didn't pick a single lock.
They walked in through a door we trusted.
The payroll vendor got breached. Their connection into us is carrying the attacker.
Same vendor with the open findings. The one we signed off.
It's the old Kestrel Pay platform. The piece we folded in and never rebuilt.
The weak spot came over with the acquisition.
A library inside our customer app was tampered with upstream.
It shipped in a release months ago. It's been phoning out ever since.
They're pulling customer records. Slowly, so nobody notices.
I'm on the bridge. Pick the first move. We argue about the second one later.
Cut it off. Whatever they came through, sever it now.
Severing. Something downstream is going to break loudly.
Don't tip them off yet. Watch where they go first.
Watching. Every minute we watch, they're still reading.
Get Elena on the phone before anything changes.
She'll ask what you did about it. Have something to say.
No answer, so I'm pulling the plug. Stop me if that's wrong.

scenes.shot_notes: A phone rattles beside a cold mug on the counter. Sam fills the screen from a dark war room, energy drink in hand, while Marcus joins by speaker.

scenes.name: The War Room

say: I pulled what I could. I won't swear that's everyone.
The ticket shows the password in plain text.
Profiles changed. Payees changed. This was not a tour.
Dana will ask who we told. Have an answer.
Talk. What did they touch, and what did you stop?
Logs first. Then the story, short.
Good. I hate a story that outruns the evidence.
It's contained. Customers come before the postmortem.
Contained is a claim. Show me where it ends.
Small mess. We can keep it inside the building.
Quiet is how a small mess becomes a resignation.
Fine. I'll tell Elena you went quiet, and I'll use the logs.
Elena hears this before the board does.
Do we freeze profile edits, or only the bad accounts?
Freeze every profile edit until we clear them.
Broad freeze. Support will howl. I can live with it.
Freeze only the accounts we know they touched.
Tighter. Miss one, and a customer tells us first.
Leave edits open. I want the next move on screen.
Bold. I'll watch. I don't have to like it.
No order. I'll freeze the touched accounts and say so.

scenes.shot_notes: Sam paces under a wall of session logs. Marcus sets down a coffee. You arrive in weekend clothes as Dana comes through the glass door.

scenes.name: The War Room

say: I ran the logs back. It's been answering with customer data for weeks.
Balances. Addresses. Account notes. Whatever a question brushed against.
Its connector reads the whole customer records share. Nobody scoped it.
Security signed off on this. I have the email.
Talk. What leaked, to whom, and is it still leaking?
Logs first. What it read, who asked, where it went.
Good. Evidence first. Feelings can wait their turn.
I signed off without a review. That's the first fact.
Hard to say out loud. Easier than having it found.
One customer, one post. Let's keep this in the building.
One post is the part we can see. Try again.
Then Sam briefs me, and you listen.
Elena gets this before the board does.
Whatever we did this morning has to hold. What stays dark until Monday?
The whole assistant stays off until we know what it read.
Every team I promised it to is about to call me.
Keep the chat. Cut every connection to customer data.
Narrow cut. If we missed a connector, we hear about it fast.
Leave it running. I want to see what it reaches for.
Watching costs customers. I'll log every answer it gives.
No call, so I'm cutting the connectors and writing that down.

scenes.location: The incident war room, Harborline Financial, Saturday noon
scenes.shot_notes: Sam scrolls a wall of chat logs. Marcus sets down a coffee. Priya stands by the glass with her arms crossed as Dana walks in.

scenes.name: The War Room

say: Here's the map. Every partner, every feed, every library we pull in.
Longer list than anyone in this building could recite.
We know one door. I can't promise it's the only one.
Talk. What did they get, and what's still open?
Facts first. What we've confirmed, then what we haven't.
Good. I can repeat confirmed. I can't repeat hopeful.
We've got a handle on it. Let's focus on the response.
A handle is a feeling. Show me where it ends.
Let's keep this in the room until we know more.
Quiet buys you a day. Then it costs you the job.
Fine. I'll brief Elena from Sam's notes. Your name goes on them anyway.
Now the hard part. What do we cut off?
Every outside link, just the bad one, or nothing until we're sure?
Cut every outside link. We bring them back one at a time.
Payroll, card feeds, all of it dark. Monday's going to scream.
Cut only the one we know. Keep the business running.
Surgical. If there's a second door, we find out the hard way.
Leave it all up. Pull the plug now and we lose our view of them.
Your call. I'll be staring at it all night.
No call. I'm cutting the one we know and logging that I chose.

scenes.location: The incident war room, Saturday noon
scenes.shot_notes: Sam paces under a wall-sized map of outside connections. Marcus sets down two coffees. You arrive in weekend clothes as Dana comes through the glass door.

scenes.name: Counsel

say: Pretended to be IT. Got a password. Used our own tool.
Customer accounts were changed. That creates duties.
Call the FBI, hire forensics, or stay inside.
Whatever you pick, I'll write it into the record.
She wants an answer today. Not a committee.
Call the FBI. We don't sit on this.
I'll place the call with you there. No side channels.
Outside forensics first. Then we choose who to call.
A clean image beats a fast story. I'll hire a firm.
Keep it internal. We investigate it ourselves.
Then the record shows we went it alone. Notice still goes out.
No decision is still a decision. I escalate at dusk.

scenes.shot_notes: Nadia squares a legal pad on the table. Dana stands at the window. No laptops are open.

scenes.name: Counsel

say: No intruder. Our own tool handed out customer data.
That doesn't shrink our duties. Customers and regulators still have to hear it.
The contract may let the vendor keep prompts. I'm reading that clause tonight.
Three paths. Law enforcement, outside forensics, or we stay inside.
Law enforcement for our own software? If you pick it, say why.
Call the FBI. We don't know who else was mining it.
Thin for a crime. The record will show we reached out anyway.
Outside forensics first. Map the exposure, then we notify.
Good. I can't file a notice on a guess. I'll hire a firm.
Our tool, our data. We handle it inside.
Customers were exposed. Inside isn't a legal option. I'm noting that you asked.
No answer by dusk, and I make the calls myself.

scenes.location: The legal room, Harborline Financial, Saturday afternoon
scenes.shot_notes: Nadia squares a legal pad and a printed vendor contract. Dana leans on the window ledge. No laptops are open.

scenes.name: Counsel

say: Someone else's weakness. Our customers' data. Our name on the letter.
The contract may say who pays. It won't say who customers blame.
And I have a signed exception for that vendor sitting in my files.
And Kestrel's old risk notes came over in the deal binder.
And the release record says that library was never reviewed.
Three paths. Call the FBI, bring in outside forensics, or keep it inside.
She needs an answer today. Not a committee.
Call the FBI. Whoever did this probably hit others the same way.
I'll place the call with you in the room. No side channels.
Outside forensics first. Then we decide who to call.
Evidence before opinions. I'll retain a firm under privilege tonight.
Keep it internal. We clean this up ourselves.
Then I'm writing down that we chose to go it alone. Notice still goes out.
Silence is an answer too. I take this to Elena at five.

scenes.shot_notes: Nadia squares a legal pad on the table. Dana stands at the window. No laptops are open.

scenes.name: The CEO

say: I know the admin tool left our control.
Did customers lose money, trust, or both?
Accounts were changed. Assume money and trust.
Then we speak early. No clever drafting.
We cut the path. The bleeding has stopped.
Stopped is not finished. Stay with it.
We don't know the full harm yet. I won't guess.
Good. I prefer a late fact to an early fable.
I called for a director, not a pause. Answer.

scenes.shot_notes: Elena fills the laptop screen from a dim kitchen, coat off, voice level, eyes not leaving the camera.

scenes.name: The CEO

say: I've read the post. I've read Priya's note.
How many customers, and did anyone lose money?
It could read the whole records share. Assume it's wide.
Then we plan for wide and hope we're wrong.
It can't reach the records now. The leak has stopped.
Stopped tonight. I still need a count by Monday.
I don't have a count. I won't make one up.
Good. A wrong number travels farther than a late one.
You run my security. I need words, not a face.
Priya says security approved this tool. Monday, I want that story straight.

scenes.location: Elena's office, seen on a video call, Saturday evening
scenes.shot_notes: Elena sits at her desk in a weekend sweater, the post open on a second monitor, eyes on the camera.

scenes.name: The CEO

say: Dana says it came through someone we trusted.
I don't care whose door it was yet. What did our customers lose?
Customer records left the building. Assume trust went with them.
Then we tell them early, in our own words.
The path is closed. Nothing's leaving now.
Closed tonight. I'll want proof it stays closed.
We don't know how much yet. I won't guess on a call.
Good. A guess on a call becomes a headline by morning.
I called my security director, not a screensaver. Talk to me.

scenes.location: Your apartment, Saturday evening, Elena on a video call
scenes.shot_notes: Elena fills the laptop screen from a dim kitchen, coat still on, eyes never leaving the camera.

scenes.name: The Board

say: Director. Short version. What happened to my customers?
Skip the diagram unless it saves the bank.
They posed as IT, moved accounts, and we cut access.
Plain words. Stay in that voice.
Help desk was fooled. The admin tool did the damage.
I heard the method. Tell me the risk.
An agent failed. Put this on that employee.
A name is not a control. Fix the door.
If you won't brief us, I'll brief them myself.
The board heard you. Now live with that sentence.

scenes.shot_notes: Richard sits at the head of the table, glasses low. Dana slides you a single sheet while the rest of the board waits.

scenes.name: The Board

say: Director. Whose data got out, and why could a chatbot see it?
I'm told the FBI got a call. About our own software?
Counsel says you wanted this kept inside. We'll come back to that.
Skip the architecture. Tell me if it happens again.
A tool read customer files it shouldn't. We cut it off and we're telling customers.
Its connector inherited staff permissions to the customer records share.
I heard plumbing. Tell me the exposure.
IT rushed it out on a deadline. The vendor built it loose.
And who signed the approval? It's in this packet.
Silence from security. I'll have that noted in the minutes.
The minutes will keep that answer longer than any of us.

scenes.location: The boardroom, Harborline Financial, Monday morning
scenes.shot_notes: Richard sits at the head of the table, glasses low, a printed screenshot under his hand. Priya sits two chairs down. Dana slides you a single sheet.

scenes.name: The Board

say: Director. I'm told we got robbed through someone else's door.
Short version. What happened, and what does it cost us?
We trusted an outside piece. It failed. We cut it off, and customers come first.
Let me walk the path, hop by hop, from their system to our data.
I heard the route. I still don't know the risk.
This is on them. Their people failed, not ours.
We chose them. A board can't outsource its own judgment.
If you won't brief this board, Dana will. Remember that.
They'll quote whatever you said first. Every single time.

scenes.shot_notes: Richard sits at the head of the table, glasses low. Dana slides you a single sheet while the rest of the board waits.

scenes.name: The Statement

say: Statement goes out before dinner. Pick the version.
Full account. Limited facts. Or no public word.
Saying nothing is still a choice. Make it.
Publish the full account. Rumors are already moving.
Then we own the pen. Send it.
Limited facts. What we know, and what we're doing.
I'll cut every adjective. The facts can stay.
No public statement. We handle it inside.
Then the first story belongs to someone else.
You froze. I'll send the limited facts and note the gap.

scenes.shot_notes: Elena stands with her coat still on. Nadia holds a printed statement flat in both hands. The screen behind them is blank.

scenes.name: The Statement

say: That post has a lot of company now. We answer tonight.
Full account, limited facts, or no public word.
Name the assistant and every bank in town reads it.
Full account. Our tool, our mistake, and what we're doing now.
Send it. We tell this one in our own words.
What we know, who's affected, and what we shut off.
Clean. I'll strip anything that sounds like a promise.
No statement. We contact customers privately.
The screenshot is already public. Silence answers it badly.
Clock's out. Limited facts go out, and I log who didn't choose.

scenes.location: A glass conference room, Harborline Financial, Monday afternoon
scenes.shot_notes: Nadia holds a printed draft flat in both hands. Elena stands with her coat on. Priya stares at the screenshot on the wall screen.

scenes.name: The Statement

say: Customer letters go out tomorrow. The public statement goes tonight.
Full account, limited facts, or nothing public.
And if we point at anyone else, we'd better be right.
Full account. Including the part where we trusted the wrong thing.
Hard to read. Harder to attack. Send it.
What happened, what we did, what customers should do. Nothing else.
Clean. I'll strip the adjectives and keep the verbs.
No public statement. We handle it with customers directly.
Then a reporter writes our first paragraph for us.
The clock beat you. I'm sending limited facts and noting who froze.

scenes.shot_notes: Elena stands with her coat still on. Nadia holds a printed draft flat in both hands. A muted news channel glows on the wall behind them.

scenes.name: The Garage

say: Year nine. Saturday still knows your number.
The desk did what helpful people do. They helped.
The board likes a villain. Don't hand them one.
We train that desk. Shame won't close a hole.
Look at that. A director who fixes the work.
New rule. No reset without a callback to the person.
Simple. Annoying. Those are the rules that survive.
HR can deal with the agent. I have a breach.
You can do both. A scarecrow is an easy fire.
Drink the coffee. The fix can wait until morning.
That's fatigue. I know the sound.

beats.caption: The admin tool stays dark until it grows a second lock.
Customers get a straight note, a careful one, or nothing at all.

say: Boards remember the sentence you led with. So do I.

scenes.shot_notes: Marcus leans on a pillar with two coffees. You take one. Your phone lights with Dana's name as the garage hums.

scenes.name: The Stairwell

say: Everybody's asking what broke. You already know.
Priya asked for a fast yes. Somebody gave her one.
The tool did exactly what it was allowed to do.
Every new AI tool gets a review. I'll teach the teams to run it.
Teaching it is how the fix outlives you. Good.

options.t: Own it and fix the gate

say: That yes was mine. Nothing touches customer data without a data map.
Owning it and fixing it. That's a rare pair.
Priya set the deadline. I just didn't fight it.
The deadline was hers. The signature was yours.
Drink the coffee. The answer won't change by morning.
That's fatigue. I know the sound.

beats.caption: The assistant stays dark until someone maps every file it can read.
Customers get a letter. Some of them keep it.

say: Priya asked who reviews the next tool. I gave her your name.

scenes.location: The parking garage stairwell, Harborline Financial, Monday night
scenes.shot_notes: Marcus sits on the stairs with two coffees. You take one. The garage lights hum and your phone lights with Dana's name.

scenes.name: The Garage

say: Nine years in, and Saturday still has your number.
So. Root cause. Not the attacker. The decision.
That vendor had open findings when you signed them off.
An exception with no end date isn't an exception. It's the policy.
Kestrel had a known hole back then. Everyone said they'd fix it after launch.
Nobody owns a promise once the company gets sold.
That library looked wrong, and the release shipped before anyone checked.
Deadlines are real. So is the code we never read.
You trusted something because checking it was slow. Everybody does. So what now?
A real third-party program. Every outside piece gets an owner and a review date.
Boring. Expensive. Exactly what would have caught this.

options.t: Teach the team what you skipped

say: I teach the team what I skipped. Out loud, my own mistake first.
That's how a scar turns into somebody else's habit.
That call came from above me. Let them own it.
Your name's on it too, kid. Own your half.
Drink the coffee. You'll know the answer by morning. You already do.
That's fatigue. I know the sound.

beats.caption: The door that let them in stays shut until someone can vouch for it.
Customer letters go out Tuesday, plain or careful.

say: You'll be asked about this Saturday for years. Keep one honest sentence ready.

scenes.location: The parking garage stairwell, Monday night
scenes.shot_notes: Marcus sits on the stairs with two coffees and hands one up. Your phone lights with Dana's name and keeps buzzing.

end: Saturday is contained. The sentence you chose stays on the record.

ends.text: The door you trusted is shut. The corner you cut is on the record.
The leak is closed. The yes that opened it is still yours.
Saturday is contained. The sentence you chose stays on the record.
